profile_text.body:
The material here is thin and, in one respect, mismatched: the harvested website text describes the DOI Foundation, not a Stanford research team. The DOI Foundation describes itself as a not-for-profit organization that governs the Digital Object Identifier (DOI) system on behalf of the agencies that manage DOI registries, and as the registration authority for the ISO standard (ISO 26324) for the DOI system. It says it is governed by its Registration Agencies and describes itself as an international community of communities spanning entertainment, standards, the built environment, natural history collections, scholarly communications, and research data. The site also notes that Jonathan Clark, Managing Agent of the DOI Foundation since 2015, died on August 11, 2026.

The only product recorded is Tutor CoPilot (Stanford research), listed under Education & Research AI. It is described as providing real-time suggestions to tutors, as not a commercial product, and as not for sale, cited as a research model. No price, privacy terms, or student age range apply per that record. Its listed URL is a DOI link resolving to an arXiv paper.

No lawsuits, SEC filings, patents, or MCP servers are present in the data.
